source.title: Plants shift gene activity within minutes of entering spaceflight, experiment reveals

key_claim: Arabidopsis plants changed their gene activity within minutes of entering spaceflight, and their responses kept changing through each phase of a short suborbital flight.

slides.headline: Plants react to space within minutes
A scientist flew with the plants
slides.body: Rob Ferl carried dozens of Arabidopsis plants in special tubes and used them at four points in the flight.

slides.headline: Over 1,200 genes changed activity
slides.body: Researchers found more than 1,200 genes whose activity changed during the flight. Leaves and roots responded differently, and so did different phases of the mission.

slides.headline: Adapting to space isn't one step
slides.body: Many of the genes help plants handle stress. The results suggest adjusting to space is a gradual process, with different responses during launch, microgravity, descent and return.

slides.headline: Adapting to space starts almost instantly.
slides.body: Plants kept changing their responses at each stage of the flight.

caption:
Plants react to space within minutes

A University of Florida team sent Arabidopsis plants on a short commercial suborbital flight. Researcher Rob Ferl rode along and preserved samples at four points: before launch, in microgravity, on descent and at landing.

The catch? Adapting to space is not one adjustment made after arriving. More than 1,200 genes changed activity, and leaves and roots responded differently across phases.

The payoff? The plants' responses kept changing as the flight went on. Preserving samples along the way let scientists see the transition itself, not just the before and after. 🌱

Source: Phys.org — Plants shift gene activity within minutes of entering spaceflight, experiment reveals
